Expanding the Urban Design Toolbox: Counter-Mapping for Gender Inclusion

2026-07-28 Springer Nature (Urban Design International) counter-mapping, feminist GIS, gender inclusion, urban design, University of Calgary, accessibility, safety, care infrastructure, participatory mapping
Read the source article

Quick summary

A University of Calgary study introduces a gender-inclusive urban design toolkit using feminist GIS and counter-mapping to identify, map, and analyze features that mainstream mapping overlooks—translating everyday experiences of safety, accessibility, and care into actionable urban design knowledge.

Key takeaways

  • The study adopts a counter-mapping approach grounded in feminist GIS to map urban design-inclusive features across the University of Calgary campus
  • Mainstream mapping practices privilege standardized, easily obtainable data, leaving women's everyday mobility needs and care infrastructures underrepresented
  • The researchers introduce a gender-inclusive urban design toolkit comprising a geospatial data typology, mapping practices, and analysis methods
  • The project produced the "UCalggary Map for All," an interactive map application for campus navigation, plus a spatial assessment of campus gender inclusivity
  • The study argues that feminist GIS can move urban design beyond conventional notions of efficient mapping toward more careful, creative, and inclusive practices
